title: Dundon's letter, the Bell firing and a Moda Center promise

chapters.headline: Dundon's letter, the Bell firing and a Moda Center promise: is the owner losing the room?
A big year for Scoot Henderson and Ja Morant's role in a crowded backcourt
Verstappen wins the Bahrain GP in Malaysia, and the engine regs take the blame for the farce
Man City found guilty on 114 charges: what punishment, and what it means for Spurs and everyone else
Oregon-UCLA: is Dante Moore back, or is it Raiola's time?

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Jack. You know it's a ten o'clock tip your time, right? For a preseason game.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: I did the math. I've got a pot of coffee and a granola bar I don't trust.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: You don't trust a granola bar.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: It came out of a hotel lobby in August. It's been in my bag ever since. It's been to three cities.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: That bar's seen more of the country than I have since I moved back.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: It's earned a game. What's the scene at your place?

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: So the bartender put a board up. Over/under on Dame's minutes tonight, nineteen and a half. People are betting wings on it.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: On a preseason game.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: On a preseason game. I took the under. The coaching staff isn't crazy. But I might not even be at the bar. My dad called and asked if I'd come over tonight.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: On a Wednesday?

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: On a Wednesday. Sundays are our thing. He has never once asked for a Wednesday.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Huh. You going?

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: I'm going. The bartender's going to text me Dame's minutes like it's a medical update. Anyway, my dad also forwarded me the letter. No note. Just the forward.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: A forward with no note is a review.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Ha. One star. Okay, the line that got me comes right before the track record one. "I'm still getting to know Portland and this fanbase." Hotels, two-way guys' travel, the layoffs, Calabro walking out the door, a broadcaster hired and fired the same day. And you're still getting to know us?

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: I mean, it's probably true.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: That's what makes it bad!

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: The Raleigh line I'd have cut. You don't bring photos of your old girlfriend on the first date. And "my track record speaks for itself" is a guy answering a question nobody put in the email.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: So is he rattled?

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: I go back and forth. I read the arena paragraph twice and kept landing on "Our focus is the long term." "We'll keep pushing until we get there." They're stuck on rent, ticket taxes, property taxes, union labor. My read is he's playing for leverage. You don't promise a long lease while you're still haggling over rent.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Okay, but look who he sent it to. Season ticket holders. Those are the people sitting at the kitchen table right now with the renewal form. There's one question on that form, and it's whether there's a team here in 2031. He answered with "long term."

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Hm.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: If he's using us to lean on the state, fine. But he just told his best customers he won't say the word "stay."

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Huh. I hadn't thought of that. So the leverage costs him with the exact people he's writing to.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: With the people who already paid! The lease runs out in 2030. Put Portland and stay in one sentence or don't hit send.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Okay, I'll move on that. I still think it's leverage. It's just leverage he's paying for out of the wrong pocket.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: And then Bell asks to come back, and the answer's "We wish Mr. Bell the best."

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: A no in a nice shirt.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Ha. Yeah. And I think the no was right. Limbo would've been worse for everybody, him included. I just don't want anybody piling on the guy. The building skipped the homework. He didn't hire himself.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Agreed. And now it's Miles, Draper or Winer. For me that's the real test this week. Pick a voice people trust inside ten minutes and a lot of this gets quiet. Go cheap again and the story writes itself.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Somebody who sounds like he's staying.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Ha. Everything with you comes back to staying.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: It's a good theme! So, tonight. Is Moda mad or happy?

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: I was going to ask you.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Both? If Dame hits one from the logo and Ja does something dumb in transition, half the city forgives a lot for two hours. I'm in that half. I know that's not healthy.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: In my experience a win buys about a week. The arena's still sitting there on Thursday.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: A week in October. In April, a win buys you a summer. That's my real fear with this guy. He needs the team good enough that nobody looks upstairs.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Speaking of the logo. Did you see the Fan Fest stuff? Dame made the whole team film dance videos walking in, and anybody who didn't do it had to dance on the court afterward.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Because there are no rookies to sing karaoke this year. I love that so much. That's a thirty-six-year-old making sure the locker room still feels like one.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: And Ja with the 360 layup.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: And the halfcourt shot to break the tie, and telling everybody he's dunking again. I read that and grinned like an idiot at my kitchen counter.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Okay, here's what I actually want to know. Where do Scoot's minutes come from? Dame plays. Ja plays. Jrue's Jrue. That's a lot of guards ahead of the kid.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Yeah.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: And everybody's "high priority" in October.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Sure. But here's what stuck with me about him. He's a combo guy, and he looks great until he's in a crowd going faster than he can think. That's Scoot. And that's a craft thing. Craft gets fixed.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Okay, but the backcourt is the crowd. Three guards who want the ball, and a kid who gets in trouble in a crowd.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: So put him with Jrue on the second unit. Jrue's the adult, Scoot runs. Nobody in his way but the other team's bench.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: And Ja?

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: My dad has exactly one ask for this season. Jrue on the floor at the end of games. So Ja off the bench? He'd sign that tonight. In two languages.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Ha. And you?

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Me, I still want Dame and Ja figuring each other out in the first six minutes. But honestly, part of me hears my dad and thinks, you want the guy you trust out there at the end. He's not wrong about much.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: If I'm the coach, I'd do it. A healthy Ja running a second unit is the best luxury in the league. The problem is whose ego can handle being told that, and I don't think it's his.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: So who loses minutes? Because you're about to say Scoot.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: I'm saying Scoot, and I don't love saying it. Follow the money. If he's a second-unit guy this year, why pay him now? Watch him for a year, pay him next summer.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Because he'll be better next summer and cost more!

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Walk me through that. You're sure he's better?

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: By March? Yeah. He looks like a guy who finally stopped carrying the whole offense up a flight of stairs every trip. Okay, that's the optimism talking. But I'll put it down. He signs before the deadline.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: I'll take the other side. Deadline passes, everybody says nice things, they sort it out next summer. Loser buys wings.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Deal. Not off the board, though. The bartender's got those riding on Dame.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Can I make a case for Sidy for one second?

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: You get one second.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Seventy-five games last year. The shot's rough, but he sticks to his guy and he's forward-sized, which is the thing we're thin on. Krejci's the shooter who has to actually start shooting.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: So Krejci shoots or he's a towel guy.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Brutal. Fair. And Yang at Fan Fest looked like he finally knew where he was supposed to stand. One scrimmage, I know.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: I'll believe Yang in March. Clingan's the five till somebody takes it.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: And Sharpe's out till about March, so nobody gets to fix the logjam with him. That one stings.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Can I say something? I kind of get Scoot right now. Twenty-two, and everybody's measuring you on somebody else's clock.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Says the independent advisor.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Says the independent advisor. Yeah. Some weeks the phone's quiet and I'm running the same math on myself.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: For what it's worth, I'd extend you.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Ha. Before the deadline?

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Before the deadline.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: You know who else was on somebody else's clock this year? Max. He thinks about walking away, signs the new deal last month, and Sunday he wins.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: You were up for it?

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Midnight start, my time. And then I sat there for a hundred minutes while the whole grid basically restarted like a laptop.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Max on the radio, laughing. "Lol, look at this."

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: I laughed out loud, alone in my apartment. And Hamilton calling it the Lego race. Five cars wide on the straight because nobody knew if they were allowed to pass. Best bad day I've ever watched in a sport this expensive.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: What gets me is how ordinary the cause was. Some rain, a slow formation lap, the software decides you don't really want power, and the whole field parks. The fix was a patch they wrote during the delay.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: In like twenty minutes. Credit there.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Sure, but they'd barely run in the wet all year. Nobody tested the one weather that was always coming to Malaysia. To me that's a management problem.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Mm, no. I mean, partly. But if my car stalled every time I eased off the gas in the rain, I'd return it. More testing days don't fix that.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Okay, both. A bad engine, and nobody checked the bad engine in the rain.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: That I'll sign.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Poor Russell, though. Engine dies late while he's running third, and that's a podium gone.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Singapore. The one track where nobody can pass. That's a parking ticket on the way out of a funeral.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Ha. Okay, Red Bull. Real?

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Real. Their own engine, first year, miserable start, and they just kept fixing it. That's my favorite kind of story. And they showed his dad on the podium looking emotional and... I don't know. Given my week, that got me a little.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Yeah. I bet.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: I think it's real too, but Sepang flattered them. Hot, rough track, half the field out of its window.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: So what would make you buy it?

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Singapore. Different demands, sprint weekend. If they're fighting up front there, I'm in. My guess is they don't win it.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Podium for Max. Minimum.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: And Hamilton. Eighteenth to third after Ferrari put him on slicks on a damp track.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: And then he's the one on the radio telling them to stay out and gamble, and it works. That's a veteran who knows exactly how much he's got left and spends every bit of it.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: City, then.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: A hundred and fourteen out of a hundred and fifteen. You'd think I'd feel better.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: You don't?

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: We're at the bottom, Jack, and it's ugly. We spent like grown-ups all summer, and a guilty verdict doesn't get us a point at Old Trafford on Saturday.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: And it's slow. The appeal gets heard around mid-December, a decision maybe end of January, and only then do they even get to the punishment.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: And the betting markets have City actually going down now. A month ago I'd have laughed.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: So, the money. Spurs reserved the right to go after City for compensation. Other clubs did too.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Okay, I have to own something. Friday I said I cared more about the league admitting the table was wrong than about any money. I've moved.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: What moved you?

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Stay with me here. The retired guy at the bar, the one who won't talk about 2007. Somebody asked him once, if the league handed you a piece of paper saying it should've gone different, would you want it? He just shrugged. Like, what would I do with that? Went back to his beer.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Ha.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: And he's right. Paper doesn't give you the nights back. Spurs finished below City, and that's real Champions League money. Players we didn't buy. So send the bill.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Look at you.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Don't. I'll make you eat the granola bar.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: My worry is whether anybody at Spurs wants the fight. Levy's gone, and he might've loved this one. The new CEO was at Arsenal back then. And they've hired a bunch of people out of City's group.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: That's the part that makes me cold. If they let it slide because it's awkward at the office, they're treating fans like a line item.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: I'd push back a little. Nobody has to decide anything until the sanction lands. And the four of them can go in together and split the lawyers.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Four guys holding one umbrella. Okay. I like that.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: But you're dodging my real question. What's broken on the field? They spent. They're bottom.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Honestly? I don't know. I want it to be confidence, one result and it flips, because it's mostly the same guys as last spring. But I watch them and I can't name the thing. That scares me more than City does.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: That's the most honest Spurs take you've ever given me.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Enjoy it. Saturday I'm irrational again.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: My turn to be irrational. Oregon-UCLA.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: How are you holding up?

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Badly. I've refreshed Ducks injury news more than my email this week. Dante Moore practiced Monday. Helmet, shoulder pads, throwing. That's all there is, and I have it memorized.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: The thing I can't get past is that the kid tried to slide. He did the smart thing and still got hit late and left in an ambulance. You don't get cute with that.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: I'd sit him. Unless the injury report says he's fully cleared, and even then I'd lean Raiola.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: I'm with you. And Reddit's already halfway to saying Moore makes bad decisions and Raiola should keep the job.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Moore has zero interceptions.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Zero! Name one bad decision!

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Ha. But Raiola was good, though. Nineteen of twenty-five, 289 yards, two touchdowns for Raiola. Off the bench, on the road.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Which is the best case for patience. The backup can run the thing, so nobody has to rush the starter. That's what a program looks like when it actually develops people.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: And here's the piece I like. Oregon's scored on every red zone trip this year, and UCLA's red zone defense is one of the worst in the country. Whoever's back there, once they get close, it's points.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Okay, that settles my stomach a little. I was ready to panic about their run game.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: I'd still keep an eye on the run game. You can be a little worried.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Also, think about Raiola for a second. If he starts Saturday, next week is Nebraska. His old team.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Oh, that's a good week to be him.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Second shot, came in cold on a bad night, played like he belonged. Whatever happens, I'm happy for that kid.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: So we agree. Moore waits till he's right, Raiola's fine, and today's injury report tells us the rest.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: We agree. Write it down, it won't happen again.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Hey. Before you go. The Wednesday thing.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Yeah. Honestly, it got me a little. He's never needed company for a game in his life. And now he calls on a Wednesday, and I'm sitting here wondering what he's not saying.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Maybe nothing. Maybe he just wants his kid on the couch for the first one with Dame back. Either way, you go, you sit there, and you stay off your phone.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Not even for the minutes?

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Fine. Once. For the minutes.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Deal. Go eat your three-city granola bar. Warriors at ten your time.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Tell Ken I said hi. Take care, Tom.
